findings.issue_text: [BUG] Changing {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to single-brace {0} placeholders plus a {2,choice,...} java.text.MessageFormat pattern breaks the React i18n interpolation used by the account UI. react-i18next only substitutes {{n}}-style placeholders, so users see the literal string 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' with raw braces and the un-evaluated choice pattern instead of the formatted message.

[BUG] The admin UI English resource now uses {0}/{1}/{2} and a {2,choice,...} MessageFormat pattern where the admin UI's i18n pipeline expects {{0}}-style interpolation. The error-invalid-multivalued-size message renders with literal braces and an unparsed choice-format fragment in the admin console attribute-validation error instead of the substituted values and singular/plural word.

[BUG] The Lithuanian translation of totpStep1 is replaced with Italian text 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users of the account console see an Italian sentence on the TOTP setup page; the translation regressed from correct Lithuanian to a wrong-language string.

[ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml derives the English sibling file purely by string replaceAll on the absolute path ('resources-community'→'resources' and locale-suffix→'_en.properties') and throws a raw RuntimeException when that guessed path does not exist. Any message file whose English counterpart does not live at the mechanically-derived path (e.g. a locale file in a directory with no matching 'resources' sibling, or a file named without a recognized locale suffix that still contains an underscore) crashes the verifier with an uncaught RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException, failing the build with a stack trace rather than a diagnosable message; contributors adding a new locale file in a new theme directory are bitten.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue's escaping of per-key exceptions (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) is a hardcoded key-name allowlist that must be extended by hand for every future key containing angle brackets. The next translator or developer adding a message key with legitimate '<' or '>' content (a URL in text, a placeholder like '<username>') gets a false 'Illegal HTML' build failure and must discover and patch this private allowlist; the per-key branches also only cover the exact spellings known today, so a key present in some locales but renamed later silently re-trips the verifier.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation is replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account console TOTP setup page see an Italian sentence; the diff's stated purpose (fixing sanitizer violations) was used to smuggle in a wrong-language replacement, and no reviewer note or test catches it.

[BUG] The English reference file is derived by blind string substitution ('resources-community'->'resources', regex-replacing the locale suffix) and a miss throws an unchecked RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException or a collected message. Any message file whose path does not follow that exact layout (community-only themes, nonstandard locale suffixes, or a *_en file whose derived sibling path resolves to a directory) crashes the whole Maven build with 'unable to read file' rather than being reported, breaking the verifier on exactly the themes it is meant to check.

[BUG] error-invalid-multivalued-size was converted to Java MessageFormat choice syntax ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}) with no verification that the JS account-ui message formatter supports choice patterns, and no test in the diff exercises the new string. The account-ui is a JavaScript app; if its formatter only handles plain {n} substitution (ICU/react-intl plural syntax differs from java.text.MessageFormat choice), users submitting an attribute with the wrong number of values see the raw choice expression or an unformatted string instead of a pluralized message.

[BUG] Only the English error-invalid-multivalued-size was rewritten to the new {0}/{1}/{2} placeholders; every non-English properties file still carrying the old {{0}}-style value for this key is left untouched by this diff. Non-English users trigger the size-validation error and see literal braces / non-substituted placeholders because the translations were never migrated to the new format the diff introduces.

[ADVISORY] The key-specific normalization whitelist in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) and the email RTL style strip are new non-trivial branches with no test coverage in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest. The four tests added cover only duplicate keys, an illegal tag, no-HTML-when-English-has-none, and a changed anchor; a regression in the choice-pattern regex (\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}) or the RTL strip silently stops flagging real violations (or starts false-flagging every email locale), and the next contributor extending the whitelist has no executable specification of the expected behavior.

[ADVISORY] containsHtml only matches lowercase opening tags (<[a-z]+[^>]*>), so an English source containing an uppercase tag or a lone closing tag is classified as HTML-free and every translation of it is held to POLICY_NO_HTML. Translations legitimately mirroring the English markup get false 'Illegal HTML' build failures (or, inversely, uppercase markup in English is never detected as the HTML source), biting maintainers of the ~50 locale files this verifier now gates.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors compares anchors strictly pairwise (first-with-first) and breaks after the first mismatch, so a translation that reorders two legitimate anchors from the English source, or repeats one, is reported as 'Didn't find anchor tag' even though every anchor is present in the original. Translators who reorder or duplicate anchors (legal in many languages) get build failures; the check verifies anchor order, not anchor safety, which is not the stated intent.

[BUG] The English source messages themselves are never validated against the safe-HTML policy, because verifying messages_en.properties compares the bundle against itself where value == englishValue, so any HTML in the English source trivially passes. The stated intent — sanitizing translated message resources — is only half-enforced: an XSS payload introduced directly in an English properties file (the default locale rendered to every user, including the account/admin UIs touched in this diff) sails through the verifier, since containsHtml(englishValue) then also flips the policy for every translation of that key to POLICY_SOME_HTML, letting the same tags into all locales.

[BUG] A missing English-file counterpart throws a raw RuntimeException instead of adding a diagnostic to the messages list, because the derived englishFile path (replaceAll("resources-community","resources") plus the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` → `_en.properties` regex) is assumed to always exist. Any locale file whose directory has no messages_en.properties sibling (or community file with no product counterpart, since the replaceAll is a no-op for paths like js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3 that never contained 'resources-community') crashes the whole verify() run with a stack trace rather than producing the per-key report every other failure mode produces — a build abort, not a verification message.

[ADVISORY] A key that exists in the translation but is missing from the English bundle silently maps to englishValue = "", which routes it to POLICY_NO_HTML and reports 'Illegal HTML' for any stale translation that still contains allowed markup. Translators and CI triage get a misleading 'Illegal HTML' error for what is actually a stale/removed English key; the real defect (key no longer exists upstream) is masked, and the obvious fix (adding the anchor/HTML back to match a non-existent English string) is impossible.

[ADVISORY] error-invalid-multivalued-size is changed from the `{{0}}`-style placeholders to Java MessageFormat with a ChoiceFormat pattern ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}), a runtime message-format semantics change bundled into a sanitizer PR. Any consumer of these message keys that does not run full MessageFormat choice processing (the React account/admin UIs render message bundles themselves) will now display the raw `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` string to end users instead of 'value(s)'; this behavior change is not traceable to the 'add sanitizer' requirement and its blast radius across JS consumers is untested in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Dozens of translation files are rewritten to the OWASP sanitizer's exact serialization output (
→
), hard-coupling every locale file to one library's whitespace emission format. Bumping owasp-java-html-sanitizer (version pinned to 20240325.1 in misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml) changes its HTML serialization style and every one of these hand-edited files across ~20 locales fails verification simultaneously; maintainers of future translations must know the verifier's normalization quirks, not HTML correctness.

[ADVISORY] The new verifySafeHtml logic has no test for the missing-English-key path, the missing-English-file path, or the allowed-HTML-in-English path (the happy case that POLICY_SOME_HTML exists for), leaving the largest branches of the new code uncovered. A regression in getEnglishValue's MissingResourceException handling or in the resources-community → resources path remapping ships silently; the next contributor adding a theme directory layout breaks CI for all translators with the raw RuntimeException from the untested FileInputStream block.

[BUG] santizeAnchors removes anchor substrings from `value` with replaceFirst while the `matcher` continues iterating over the pre-removal string, so positions go stale and the wrong anchor can be removed. For a translation with two anchors (e.g. totpStep1 with both the FreeOTP and Google Play links), after the first replaceFirst the string shrinks but matcher.find() keeps advancing on the old offsets; the second anchor is matched against the wrong English anchor or the replaceFirst removes the first occurrence of a different anchor's text, producing spurious 'Didn't find anchor tag' / 'Illegal HTML' verifier failures on legitimate translations.

[ADVISORY] The English reference file is located by regex-munging the absolute path (`replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`) and a missing file throws a raw RuntimeException instead of being handled. Any locale file whose product-tree counterpart does not exist at the munged path (e.g. running the verifier in a checkout where only the community tree is present, or a theme present only under maven-resources-community) crashes the whole verify() run with 'unable to read file <null-ish path>' rather than skipping or reporting a per-file message — one new locale file added in the wrong tree bricks the build pipeline. The unanchored `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` also matches the first underscore segment of any directory/file name containing a dot-underscore pattern, so a single rename under themes/ silently points the check at the wrong English file.

[ADVISORY] containsHtml uses `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` which only matches lowercase tag names, so English source strings containing uppercase tags (`

`, ``, `
`) are classified as HTML-free. For such keys the code applies POLICY_NO_HTML, so every translation of that key that legitimately mirrors the uppercase or even lowercases the tag gets a false 'Illegal HTML' verifier failure the moment an English file with an uppercase tag is added — the gate fires on correct data and the contributor has no way to satisfy it.

[BUG] The Lithuanian file's totpStep1 was replaced with an Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') rather than a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users of the community account theme see the TOTP setup instruction rendered in Italian; the surrounding totpStep2/totpStep3 remain Lithuanian.

[ADVISORY] error-invalid-multivalued-size was converted from escaped `{{n}}` placeholders to live `{n}` including a `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` ChoiceFormat pattern, but the account-ui is a JS frontend whose message formatter must support Java ChoiceFormat for this to render. If the JS-side formatter used by the account UI does not implement the choice sub-format, users see the literal string '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' in the attribute validation error message; the same key exists in admin-ui messages so both renderers need verifying, and the format change is a silent contract shift for any downstream theme overriding this key.

[ADVISORY] owasp-java-html-sanitizer and commons-text are added with hardcoded versions (20240325.1, 1.13.0) directly in the misc module rather than through the parent dependencyManagement/BOM. The next person bumping shared dependency versions in the parent POM silently misses these two, so the module drifts onto stale sanitizer versions (a security-relevant library for a guard whose whole job is catching unsafe HTML) and future CVE bumps require a hunt through leaf poms.

[ADVISORY] POLICY_SOME_HTML hardcodes the allowed tag set to exactly br/p/strong/b, but this whitelist lives in the verifier rather than being derived from or shared with the actual rendering stack's allowed set. The moment a legitimate English source string introduces `<em>`, `<i>`, `<code>`, `<ul>/<li>` (common in help texts), every existing translation of that key fails the verifier simultaneously and all locales must be touched in one commit — an evolvability cliff where the guard policy and the real rendering policy are parallel hand-maintained enumerations that will drift.

[ADVISORY] The email RTL exemption is keyed on `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` and strips one hardcoded style literal, baking theme-specific data into the generic verifier. Any non-email message file whose path happens to contain 'email', or any email template using a differently formatted/whitespaced RTL style attribute (e.g. single quotes or extra spaces), either loses the exemption or keeps failing; each new exception pattern requires editing normalizeValue's if-chain — the TODO acknowledges this but the shape (growing per-key/per-path special cases in code) means every future exception is another conditional in the hot verification path.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users setting up 2FA see Italian instructions on the account console TOTP page; the PR's stated intent was sanitizing HTML in translations, not swapping in wrong-language content, and no human accepted a Lithuanian→Italian regression.

[ADVISORY] The PR's objective silently drifted from 'add a sanitizer to verify translations' to 'rewrite translations until they pass the verifier': totpStep1 in fi/lt/sk/sv/zh_CN was replaced with a link-free string that drops the FreeOTP and Google Play anchors rather than fixing the anchors to match the English source. Finnish (and Lithuanian, Slovak, Swedish, Chinese) users lose the direct download links for the authenticator apps during 2FA setup — the content change was driven by making the new tool pass, not by an accepted translation requirement.

[ADVISORY] A PR titled 'Add HTML sanitizer' silently changes the English message format from double-brace '{{0}}' MessageFormat-escaped placeholders to single-brace '{0}' plus a '{2,choice,...}' ChoiceFormat pattern in error-invalid-multivalued-size, changing runtime formatting semantics in the account UI. The rendered validation error in the account UI now depends on the frontend correctly interpreting single-brace and choice patterns (JS-based message formatting may not support MessageFormat choice syntax), producing messages with literal '{2,choice,...}' fragments; this behavior change ships unreviewed under a sanitizer-only intent.

[ADVISORY] normalizeValue grows a hardcoded per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size, email RTL style) so the 'sanitizer' is really a per-key whitelist that will silently pass unsafe content in any future key added to this list. The next contributor who hits a verifier failure will most naturally add another key to this escape hatch rather than fix the message, progressively eroding the security intent of the sanitizer; each entry is also a place the policy and the properties files must stay in sync with no test.

[ADVISORY] No test asserts the happy path — every new test asserts a violation is reported, and none asserts that a fully valid translated properties file produces an empty messages list, so a false-positive regression in the sanitizer passes the whole suite. The four new tests (verifyDuplicateKeysDetected, verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected, verifyNoHtmlAllowed, verifyNoChangedAnchors) all use hasItem(containsString(...)), which is satisfied even when the verifier spuriously flags every key. I checked VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java — no fixture or assertion anywhere asserts verify() returns an empty list for a clean translation. If a sanitizer/policy regression (e.g., containsHtml() always true, or the unescapeHtml4/replace("<!-- -->","") roundtrip drifting) starts flagging valid translations, the unit tests stay green while the theme-verifier build breaks for every locale contributor. Checked files: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java and all fixtures under misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources/.

[ADVISORY] The normalizeValue() escape-hatch branches (templateHelp's 'CLAIM.<NAME>' removal, optimizeLookupHelp's '<Extensions>' removal, and the {n,choice,...} pattern stripping for error-invalid-multivalued-size and linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit) are exercised by no test in this diff, even though the diff itself depends on them — the properties-file edits to templateHelp and error-invalid-multivalued-size only pass this verifier because of these untested regexes. A regression in any of the three hand-rolled regexes in normalizeValue (e.g., 'CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>' failing to match, or the choice pattern '[^{0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}' regex breaking) flags legitimate translations as 'Illegal HTML' in CI. The keycloak.v3/admin-ui messages_en.properties edited in this very diff contains the new choice-format string that only passes via the third branch — yet no fixture covers a key with {2,choice,...}, so the branch that this PR's own properties change relies on is verified by nothing. Checked: VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java and all five test fixtures — none contains a choice pattern, 'CLAIM.<', '<Extensions>', or an email style attribute.

[ADVISORY] The illegalHtmlTag fixture is malformed HTML (value ends '
tag...
) is detected. If the OWASP sanitizer changes how it handles unterminated tags (e.g., emitting the raw ' tag is not in the allowed set'. A maintainer changing POLICY_SOME_HTML or the unescape logic gets a test whose pass/fail depends on malformed-input parsing quirks, not the policy. Fixture should be 'Some
tag
' to test what the verifier is documented to catch.

[BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation is replaced with Italian text: 'totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users of the account console TOTP setup page see Italian instructions; the migration of translation data corrupted the row's language fidelity, replacing the prior (correct, link-carrying) Lithuanian content with a copy-paste from the Italian locale rather than a translation. This is a silent data overwrite with no rollback to the previous Lithuanian string in this diff.

[ADVISORY] totpStep1 in fi/lt/sk/sv/zh_CN is rewritten to 'install one of the following applications' while the diff removes all <a> app-store links that the English base template's FreeOTP/Google Authenticator list expects. Users of these locales get an instruction that references a list ('following applications') that the surrounding totpStep1 template markup may no longer render if the link list lives in the removed anchors, producing a confusing partial instruction; the rewrite also discards the locale-specific store links without a documented replacement source.

[BUG] The common-prefix/common-suffix stripping before building the 'Illegal HTML' message throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when the sanitized string is longer than the original with an overlapping prefix and suffix, crashing verify() instead of reporting the violation. A translation containing a raw ampersand (e.g. 'Tom & Jerry') under a key whose English value contains HTML gets its '&' escaped to '&' by the sanitizer; the prefix scan consumes the entire value (start == value.length()) while the suffix scan also finds at least one matching trailing char, so value.substring(start, value.length() - end) is called with start > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — the Maven mojo dies with a stack trace about substring rather than the 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message the tool exists to produce, and the actual HTML violation is never reported.

[BUG] Deriving the English-file path with the regex replaceAll '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' -> '_en.properties' produces a nonexistent path for any file whose locale segment contains digits or that has no locale suffix, and the subsequent failure is thrown as a raw RuntimeException instead of being collected as a verification message. For a locale file like messages_es_419.properties (or a bundle with no locale suffix), the character class [a-zA-Z-_] cannot match '419', the replacement leaves the filename unchanged or yields a path with no messages_en.properties sibling, and new FileInputStream(englishFile) throws — wrapped in a bare RuntimeException, not MojoExecutionException — so the verifier run aborts with an unexpected crash rather than either verifying the file or reporting a clean 'missing English source' finding.

[ADVISORY] santizeAnchors adds the 'Didn't find anchor tag' message and breaks, but then returns the value with only some anchors stripped, so verifySafeHtml also emits a second misleading 'Illegal HTML' entry pointing at the anchor text itself, and any anchors after the mismatch point are never checked. A translator who modifies an anchor href gets two error entries — the accurate anchor-mismatch one plus a bogus 'Illegal HTML' one naming the <a ...> tag as the illegal content — and additional divergent anchors later in the same string are silently unexamined, misdirecting the contributor fixing the translation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Changing {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} to single-brace {0} placeholders plus a {2,choice,...} java.text.MessageFormat pattern breaks the React i18n interpolation used by the account UI. react-i18next only substitutes {{n}}-style placeholders, so users see the literal string 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.' with raw braces and the un-evaluated choice pattern instead of the formatted message.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change message placeholders from double-curly `{{0}}` to single-brace `{0}` and adds a Java `MessageFormat`-style choice pattern (e.g. `error-invalid-multivalued-size=... {2,choice,...}`) in multiple `*.properties` files, including the account UI resources. However, the claim that this “breaks the React i18n interpolation used by the account UI” and that “react-i18next only substitutes {{n}} placeholders” is not verifiable from the diff: there is no React/i18next configuration or interpolation code shown. In fact, the PR adds theme-verifier logic that explicitly normalizes/accepts `choice` patterns for `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, suggesting the project expects/permits this syntax rather than it being a breaking change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The admin UI English resource now uses {0}/{1}/{2} and a {2,choice,...} MessageFormat pattern where the admin UI's i18n pipeline expects {{0}}-style interpolation. The error-invalid-multivalued-size message renders with literal braces and an unparsed choice-format fragment in the admin console attribute-validation error instead of the substituted values and singular/plural word.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the admin UI message key `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` to a standard `MessageFormat`-style `{0}/{1}/{2}` with a `{2,choice,...}` pluralization fragment (e.g., in `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties` and also in `themes/.../messages_en.properties`). Nothing in the provided diff shows the admin console i18n pipeline “expects {{0}}-style interpolation” or that `{2,choice,...}` would be left unparsed. In fact, the PR adds `theme-verifier` logic that explicitly normalizes/handles `choice` patterns for this exact key (`normalizeValue(... key.equals("error-invalid-multivalued-size") ...)`), suggesting these patterns are intended/accepted rather than broken.

Lithuanian users of the account console see an Italian sentence on the TOTP setup page; the translation regressed from correct Lithuanian to a wrong-language string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] verifySafeHtml derives the English sibling file purely by string replaceAll on the absolute path ('resources-community'→'resources' and locale-suffix→'_en.properties') and throws a raw RuntimeException when that guessed path does not exist. Any message file whose English counterpart does not live at the mechanically-derived path (e.g. a locale file in a directory with no matching 'resources' sibling, or a file named without a recognized locale suffix that still contains an underscore) crashes the verifier with an uncaught RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException, failing the build with a stack trace rather than a diagnosable message; contributors adding a new locale file in a new theme directory are bitten.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds verifySafeHtml(), which computes an English file path via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community","resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` and then opens it with `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. If that mechanically-derived path is wrong or the English file doesn’t exist, the code catches `IOException` and throws a raw `RuntimeException` (not a `MojoExecutionException`). Since `verify()` only catches `IOException` from `Files.readString(...)`, this RuntimeException will escape and crash the verifier/build with a stack trace rather than a collected/diagnostic message. The concern is directly grounded in the added code paths and exception handling shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue's escaping of per-key exceptions (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) is a hardcoded key-name allowlist that must be extended by hand for every future key containing angle brackets. The next translator or developer adding a message key with legitimate '<' or '>' content (a URL in text, a placeholder like '<username>') gets a false 'Illegal HTML' build failure and must discover and patch this private allowlist; the per-key branches also only cover the exact spellings known today, so a key present in some locales but renamed later silently re-trips the verifier.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `verifySafeHtml()` with `normalizeValue(key, value)` containing explicit per-key exceptions: `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` (see the new `if/else` chain). This is a hardcoded key-name allowlist to suppress sanitizer differences caused by non-HTML angle-bracket content (e.g., `CLAIM.<NAME>`, `<Extensions>`, MessageFormat choice patterns with `<`). Because `containsHtml()` treats `<[a-z]+...>` as HTML-like and the sanitizer compares sanitized vs original, any future message containing legitimate `<...>` text could indeed trigger a new “Illegal HTML” failure unless another special-case is added. That’s a maintainability/scope concern introduced by this change, not a current functional defect in the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 translation is replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') instead of Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account console TOTP setup page see an Italian sentence; the diff's stated purpose (fixing sanitizer violations) was used to smuggle in a wrong-language replacement, and no reviewer note or test catches it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff directly changes Lithuanian strings to Italian text. In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `totpStep1` is changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` (Italian). The same happens in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` for `loginTotpStep1`. This is a user-facing wrong-language translation introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The English reference file is derived by blind string substitution ('resources-community'->'resources', regex-replacing the locale suffix) and a miss throws an unchecked RuntimeException instead of a MojoExecutionException or a collected message. Any message file whose path does not follow that exact layout (community-only themes, nonstandard locale suffixes, or a *_en file whose derived sibling path resolves to a directory) crashes the whole Maven build with 'unable to read file' rather than being reported, breaking the verifier on exactly the themes it is meant to check.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, the English reference path is derived via blind substitutions (`replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` and `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`). It then unconditionally opens that derived path with `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`, and on any `IOException` it throws a plain unchecked `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` rather than collecting a verifier message or throwing `MojoExecutionException`. Since `verify()` only wraps `Files.readString(...)` IO failures, this unchecked exception will bubble up and can fail the whole Maven build if the derived English file doesn’t exist or resolves incorrectly (e.g., nonstandard layout/locale suffix).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] error-invalid-multivalued-size was converted to Java MessageFormat choice syntax ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}) with no verification that the JS account-ui message formatter supports choice patterns, and no test in the diff exercises the new string. The account-ui is a JavaScript app; if its formatter only handles plain {n} substitution (ICU/react-intl plural syntax differs from java.text.MessageFormat choice), users submitting an attribute with the wrong number of values see the raw choice expression or an unformatted string instead of a pluralized message.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in JS app message bundles (e.g., `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties`) from simple placeholders to a Java `MessageFormat` choice pattern: `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The diff does not show any corresponding change or verification of the JavaScript-side message formatting implementation, nor any tests that exercise rendering of this specific key with the new choice syntax (the added tests are for HTML sanitization in `theme-verifier`). Whether this is an actual runtime break depends on formatter behavior not shown in the diff, so it’s a concrete compatibility/test-gap concern rather than a provable defect from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Only the English error-invalid-multivalued-size was rewritten to the new {0}/{1}/{2} placeholders; every non-English properties file still carrying the old {{0}}-style value for this key is left untouched by this diff. Non-English users trigger the size-validation error and see literal braces / non-substituted placeholders because the translations were never migrated to the new format the diff introduces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any non-English `error-invalid-multivalued-size` entries still using the old `{{0}}` placeholder style. The only `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` forms shown are in English files being updated, and at least one non-English file (`messages_sk.properties`) is also updated for this key. Since the claim relies on other non-English files “still carrying the old {{0}}-style value” that are not present in the diff, the finding is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The key-specific normalization whitelist in normalizeValue (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size) and the email RTL style strip are new non-trivial branches with no test coverage in VerifyMessagePropertiesTest. The four tests added cover only duplicate keys, an illegal tag, no-HTML-when-English-has-none, and a changed anchor; a regression in the choice-pattern regex (\{[0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}) or the RTL strip silently stops flagging real violations (or starts false-flagging every email locale), and the next contributor extending the whitelist has no executable specification of the expected behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple key-specific branches in VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue() (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*/error-invalid-multivalued-size choice-pattern replacement, and an email-specific removal of `style="direction: rtl;"` based on file path containing "email"). The updated test class VerifyMessagePropertiesTest only adds coverage for duplicate keys, generic illegal HTML, “no HTML allowed when English has none”, and changed anchors, and does not exercise the new normalizeValue branches or the email RTL stripping. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test-coverage gap for non-trivial new logic where regressions could change sanitizer behavior or cause false positives/negatives.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] containsHtml only matches lowercase opening tags (<[a-z]+[^>]*>), so an English source containing an uppercase tag or a lone closing tag is classified as HTML-free and every translation of it is held to POLICY_NO_HTML. Translations legitimately mirroring the English markup get false 'Illegal HTML' build failures (or, inversely, uppercase markup in English is never detected as the HTML source), biting maintainers of the ~50 locale files this verifier now gates.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties, containsHtml() uses HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") and returns matcher.find(), which only detects lowercase opening tags and will not match uppercase tags (e.g.,
) or closing-only tags (e.g., ). This directly drives policy selection: PolicyFactory policy = containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML. Therefore an English string containing uppercase HTML will be misclassified as “no HTML”, causing translations that mirror the English markup to be sanitized under POLICY_NO_HTML and flagged as "Illegal HTML".

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors compares anchors strictly pairwise (first-with-first) and breaks after the first mismatch, so a translation that reorders two legitimate anchors from the English source, or repeats one, is reported as 'Didn't find anchor tag' even though every anchor is present in the original. Translators who reorder or duplicate anchors (legal in many languages) get build failures; the check verifies anchor order, not anchor safety, which is not the stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, the code iterates `matcher.find()` over anchor tags in the translated `value` and simultaneously advances `englishMatcher.find()` over the English anchors, requiring a strict first-with-first, second-with-second match (`Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`). On the first mismatch it emits "Didn't find anchor tag ..." and `break`s. This enforces identical order and count of `<a...>` tags, so a translation that reorders two legitimate anchors or repeats one will fail even if all anchor tags exist in the English source, contradicting the method comment "Allow only those anchor tags from the source key to also appear in the target key."

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The English source messages themselves are never validated against the safe-HTML policy, because verifying messages_en.properties compares the bundle against itself where value == englishValue, so any HTML in the English source trivially passes. The stated intent — sanitizing translated message resources — is only half-enforced: an XSS payload introduced directly in an English properties file (the default locale rendered to every user, including the account/admin UIs touched in this diff) sails through the verifier, since containsHtml(englishValue) then also flips the policy for every translation of that key to POLICY_SOME_HTML, letting the same tags into all locales.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `verifySafeHtml()` always sanitizes `value` and compares `sanitized` vs `value` (`if (!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)) ... messages.add("Illegal HTML...")`). Even when verifying an `_en.properties` file where `englishFile` resolves to the same file (so `value == englishValue`), disallowed tags/attributes would still be removed by OWASP sanitizer (POLICY_SOME_HTML allows only `br,p,strong,b` and no attributes; POLICY_NO_HTML allows none), making `sanitized != value` and thus triggering an error. Therefore English sources are still validated against the policy; they do not “trivially pass” just because they’re compared to themselves, and an XSS payload would not generally “sail through” under these policies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A missing English-file counterpart throws a raw RuntimeException instead of adding a diagnostic to the messages list, because the derived englishFile path (replaceAll("resources-community","resources") plus the `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` → `_en.properties` regex) is assumed to always exist. Any locale file whose directory has no messages_en.properties sibling (or community file with no product counterpart, since the replaceAll is a no-op for paths like js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3 that never contained 'resources-community') crashes the whole verify() run with a stack trace rather than producing the per-key report every other failure mode produces — a build abort, not a verification message.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, the code unconditionally derives an `englishFile` path and then loads it via `new FileInputStream(englishFile)`. If that file does not exist, the `catch (IOException e)` block throws a raw `RuntimeException` ("unable to read file ..."), which is not caught by `verify()` (it only catches `IOException` from `Files.readString`). This will abort verification/build instead of adding a message to the `messages` list, and the path derivation (`replaceAll("resources-community","resources")` and `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` -> `_en.properties`) can be a no-op or point to a non-existent sibling for some directories.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A key that exists in the translation but is missing from the English bundle silently maps to englishValue = "", which routes it to POLICY_NO_HTML and reports 'Illegal HTML' for any stale translation that still contains allowed markup. Translators and CI triage get a misleading 'Illegal HTML' error for what is actually a stale/removed English key; the real defect (key no longer exists upstream) is masked, and the obvious fix (adding the anchor/HTML back to match a non-existent English string) is impossible.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties#getEnglishValue, a missing key in the English bundle is caught and mapped to englishValue="" (MissingResourceException -> ""). verifySafeHtml then uses containsHtml(englishValue) to choose POLICY_NO_HTML when englishValue is empty, so any translation value containing markup (e.g., , ,
) will be sanitized/changed and reported as "Illegal HTML". This can misreport the root cause (stale/extra translation key not present in English) as an HTML violation, because the logic never emits a "missing English key" diagnostic and instead routes the case through the HTML sanitizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] error-invalid-multivalued-size is changed from the `{{0}}`-style placeholders to Java MessageFormat with a ChoiceFormat pattern ({2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}), a runtime message-format semantics change bundled into a sanitizer PR. Any consumer of these message keys that does not run full MessageFormat choice processing (the React account/admin UIs render message bundles themselves) will now display the raw `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` string to end users instead of 'value(s)'; this behavior change is not traceable to the 'add sanitizer' requirement and its blast radius across JS consumers is untested in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in multiple message bundles from a simple "value(s)" string (and in some places `{{0}}`-style escaping) to a Java `MessageFormat` ChoiceFormat pattern: `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` (e.g., `themes/.../messages_en.properties`, `js/apps/.../messages_en.properties`). That is a runtime message-format semantics change bundled alongside the new HTML-sanitizer verification logic (`VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue` even adds a special-case for `error-invalid-multivalued-size` because the choice format contains `<`). However, the claim that JS/React consumers will definitely render the raw `{2,choice,...}` text is not verifiable from this diff because no UI rendering/formatting code is shown. So it’s a concrete, diff-grounded scope/compatibility concern, but not a confirmed defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
[ADVISORY] Dozens of translation files are rewritten to the OWASP sanitizer's exact serialization output (
→
), hard-coupling every locale file to one library's whitespace emission format. Bumping owasp-java-html-sanitizer (version pinned to 20240325.1 in misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml) changes its HTML serialization style and every one of these hand-edited files across ~20 locales fails verification simultaneously; maintainers of future translations must know the verifier's normalization quirks, not HTML correctness.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds strict HTML sanitization verification in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` by computing `sanitized = policy.sanitize(value)` and then comparing `sanitized` vs the original `value` for exact equality (after limited unescape/cleanup). There is no normalization that would treat equivalent HTML serializations as equal (e.g., `
` vs `
`), and the PR correspondingly rewrites many locale strings to match the sanitizer’s emitted form (`
` → `
`). This makes the verifier (and thus translation files) coupled to the OWASP sanitizer’s exact serialization/canonicalization behavior rather than just HTML safety/correctness, which is a maintainability/architecture concern rather than an immediate product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new verifySafeHtml logic has no test for the missing-English-key path, the missing-English-file path, or the allowed-HTML-in-English path (the happy case that POLICY_SOME_HTML exists for), leaving the largest branches of the new code uncovered. A regression in getEnglishValue's MissingResourceException handling or in the resources-community → resources path remapping ships silently; the next contributor adding a theme directory layout breaks CI for all translators with the raw RuntimeException from the untested FileInputStream block.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new branching logic in `verifySafeHtml()`: it always tries to open an inferred English file path via `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` and throws a raw `RuntimeException` on `IOException`, and it has a missing-English-key fallback in `getEnglishValue()` (catches `MissingResourceException` and returns ""). The new tests only cover duplicate keys, illegal HTML detection, “no HTML allowed” when English has no HTML, and changed anchor detection; none cover (1) missing English key behavior, (2) missing English file / path-remapping failure (`resources-community`→`resources` and `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties`→`_en.properties`), or (3) the happy-path where English contains allowed HTML and `POLICY_SOME_HTML` should leave the translation unchanged. This is a concrete coverage gap for the largest new code paths, not a directly provable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] santizeAnchors removes anchor substrings from `value` with replaceFirst while the `matcher` continues iterating over the pre-removal string, so positions go stale and the wrong anchor can be removed. For a translation with two anchors (e.g. totpStep1 with both the FreeOTP and Google Play links), after the first replaceFirst the string shrinks but matcher.find() keeps advancing on the old offsets; the second anchor is matched against the wrong English anchor or the replaceFirst removes the first occurrence of a different anchor's text, producing spurious 'Didn't find anchor tag' / 'Illegal HTML' verifier failures on legitimate translations.

adjudication.rationale: In `santizeAnchors`, the `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` does iterate over the original `value` string, but the code never uses `matcher` offsets (start/end) against the mutated string—only `matcher.group()` (the matched tag text). After `value = value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")`, subsequent iterations still compare the next original tag text to the next English tag text, and `replaceFirst` removes the first occurrence of that exact tag text from the *current* `value`. With distinct anchors, this does not depend on matcher positions and will remove the intended tags. The described “stale offsets remove wrong anchor / spurious failures on legitimate translations” is not demonstrated by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The English reference file is located by regex-munging the absolute path (`replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`) and a missing file throws a raw RuntimeException instead of being handled. Any locale file whose product-tree counterpart does not exist at the munged path (e.g. running the verifier in a checkout where only the community tree is present, or a theme present only under maven-resources-community) crashes the whole verify() run with 'unable to read file <null-ish path>' rather than skipping or reporting a per-file message — one new locale file added in the wrong tree bricks the build pipeline. The unanchored `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` also matches the first underscore segment of any directory/file name containing a dot-underscore pattern, so a single rename under themes/ silently points the check at the wrong English file.

adjudication.rationale: In `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()`, the English reference bundle is loaded from a path derived via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. If that derived `englishFile` does not exist, the code catches `IOException` and throws a raw `RuntimeException` (`"unable to read file " + englishFile`), which is not handled by `verify()` (it only catches `IOException` from `Files.readString`). This means a missing/incorrectly-derived English file will crash the whole verification run rather than returning a per-file message or a `MojoExecutionException`, matching the finding’s core claim that one misplaced locale file can brick the build.

adjudication_records.issue_text:
[ADVISORY] containsHtml uses `Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` which only matches lowercase tag names, so English source strings containing uppercase tags (`

`, ``, `
`) are classified as HTML-free. For such keys the code applies POLICY_NO_HTML, so every translation of that key that legitimately mirrors the uppercase or even lowercases the tag gets a false 'Illegal HTML' verifier failure the moment an English file with an uppercase tag is added — the gate fires on correct data and the contributor has no way to satisfy it.

adjudication.rationale:
In VerifyMessageProperties, containsHtml() relies on `Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")`, which matches only lowercase tag names. This directly means an English source string containing uppercase HTML tags (e.g., `

`, `
`, ``) would not be detected as HTML, causing the code to select `POLICY_NO_HTML` (`containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML`). That would make any translation containing the corresponding HTML (even if correct) be sanitized/stripped and then flagged as "Illegal HTML". This is a correctness defect in the new verifier logic introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian file's totpStep1 was replaced with an Italian sentence ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:') rather than a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users of the community account theme see the TOTP setup instruction rendered in Italian; the surrounding totpStep2/totpStep3 remain Lithuanian.

adjudication.rationale: In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `totpStep1` is changed from a Lithuanian instruction with links to the Italian sentence `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` while the surrounding `totpStep2`/`totpStep3` remain Lithuanian. The same Italian string is also introduced for `loginTotpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`. This is a clear locale/translation correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] error-invalid-multivalued-size was converted from escaped `{{n}}` placeholders to live `{n}` including a `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` ChoiceFormat pattern, but the account-ui is a JS frontend whose message formatter must support Java ChoiceFormat for this to render. If the JS-side formatter used by the account UI does not implement the choice sub-format, users see the literal string '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' in the attribute validation error message; the same key exists in admin-ui messages so both renderers need verifying, and the format change is a silent contract shift for any downstream theme overriding this key.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in account-ui and admin-ui bundles from `{{0}}...value(s)` to MessageFormat-style `{0}...` and adds a Java `ChoiceFormat` fragment `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` (e.g., in `js/apps/account-ui/...messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/admin-ui/...messages_en.properties`, and similarly in base theme). However, the diff does not show how the JS UIs format messages at runtime, so we cannot confirm whether their formatter supports Java ChoiceFormat or would render the choice pattern literally. It is still a concrete contract/compatibility concern introduced by this change (including for downstream overrides), but not a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] owasp-java-html-sanitizer and commons-text are added with hardcoded versions (20240325.1, 1.13.0) directly in the misc module rather than through the parent dependencyManagement/BOM. The next person bumping shared dependency versions in the parent POM silently misses these two, so the module drifts onto stale sanitizer versions (a security-relevant library for a guard whose whole job is catching unsafe HTML) and future CVE bumps require a hunt through leaf poms.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two new dependencies added to `misc/theme-verifier/pom.xml` with explicit `<version>` tags (`owasp-java-html-sanitizer` 20240325.1 and `commons-text` 1.13.0). That is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/upgrade-risk concern because these versions will not automatically track any centrally managed versions. However, the claim that the project *does* have a parent `dependencyManagement`/BOM that should be used is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] POLICY_SOME_HTML hardcodes the allowed tag set to exactly br/p/strong/b, but this whitelist lives in the verifier rather than being derived from or shared with the actual rendering stack's allowed set. The moment a legitimate English source string introduces `<em>`, `<i>`, `<code>`, `<ul>/<li>` (common in help texts), every existing translation of that key fails the verifier simultaneously and all locales must be touched in one commit — an evolvability cliff where the guard policy and the real rendering policy are parallel hand-maintained enumerations that will drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new HTML-safety verifier that hardcodes an allowlist in `POLICY_SOME_HTML` to only `br`, `p`, `strong`, `b` (`VerifyMessageProperties.java`). The verifier decides whether to allow any HTML based on whether the English string contains an HTML tag (`containsHtml(englishValue)`), but it does not expand the allowlist based on what tags appear in English. As a result, if a legitimate English source string later uses another common tag like `<em>`/`<i>`/`<code>`/`<ul>` etc., translations containing the same legitimate tag would be sanitized (tag removed) and then flagged as `Illegal HTML`, forcing broad locale updates or a policy change. This is an evolvability/maintenance concern created by the change, not a direct functional defect in the current diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The email RTL exemption is keyed on `file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")` and strips one hardcoded style literal, baking theme-specific data into the generic verifier. Any non-email message file whose path happens to contain 'email', or any email template using a differently formatted/whitespaced RTL style attribute (e.g. single quotes or extra spaces), either loses the exemption or keeps failing; each new exception pattern requires editing normalizeValue's if-chain — the TODO acknowledges this but the shape (growing per-key/per-path special cases in code) means every future exception is another conditional in the hot verification path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `normalizeValue()` logic that treats any file whose absolute path contains the substring `"email"` specially and strips only the exact literal ` style="direction: rtl;"` (see `if (file.getAbsolutePath().contains("email")) { value = value.replaceAll(Pattern.quote(" style=\"direction: rtl;\""), ""); }`). This is a brittle, theme/path-specific exception embedded in the generic verifier and would require further conditionals for other RTL formatting variants or future exceptions, matching the finding’s architecture/maintainability concern. It’s not necessarily a current functional defect in the shown diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded issue created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Lithuanian totpStep1 was replaced with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'), not a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users setting up 2FA see Italian instructions on the account console TOTP page; the PR's stated intent was sanitizing HTML in translations, not swapping in wrong-language content, and no human accepted a Lithuanian→Italian regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Lithuanian translation files changed to Italian text: in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `totpStep1` becomes `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, and in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`, `loginTotpStep1` is changed to the same Italian sentence. This is a clear wrong-language regression visible directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR's objective silently drifted from 'add a sanitizer to verify translations' to 'rewrite translations until they pass the verifier': totpStep1 in fi/lt/sk/sv/zh_CN was replaced with a link-free string that drops the FreeOTP and Google Play anchors rather than fixing the anchors to match the English source. Finnish (and Lithuanian, Slovak, Swedish, Chinese) users lose the direct download links for the authenticator apps during 2FA setup — the content change was driven by making the new tool pass, not by an accepted translation requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows user-facing message regressions: `totpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_fi.properties`, `messages_lt.properties`, `messages_sk.properties`, `messages_sv.properties`, and `messages_zh_CN.properties` was changed from a string containing `<a href=...>` download links (FreeOTP/Google Play/App Store) to a link-free generic sentence. Additionally, Lithuanian `totpStep1` (and `loginTotpStep1` in `themes/.../login/messages/messages_lt.properties`) is replaced with Italian text ("Installa una delle seguenti...") which is clearly incorrect content for that locale. This is a concrete, diff-grounded degradation of UI text/content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A PR titled 'Add HTML sanitizer' silently changes the English message format from double-brace '{{0}}' MessageFormat-escaped placeholders to single-brace '{0}' plus a '{2,choice,...}' ChoiceFormat pattern in error-invalid-multivalued-size, changing runtime formatting semantics in the account UI. The rendered validation error in the account UI now depends on the frontend correctly interpreting single-brace and choice patterns (JS-based message formatting may not support MessageFormat choice syntax), producing messages with literal '{2,choice,...}' fragments; this behavior change ships unreviewed under a sanitizer-only intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size` from `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` placeholders to single-brace `{0}/{1}/{2}` and adds a `{2,choice,...}` pattern in multiple English properties files (e.g., `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties`, `js/apps/admin-ui/.../messages_en.properties`, and `themes/src/main/resources/.../messages_en.properties`). That is a real, potentially runtime-significant message-format semantics change, and the PR also adds sanitizer-related verification logic that explicitly special-cases choice patterns (`normalizeValue(... key.equals("error-invalid-multivalued-size") ...)`). However, the finding’s claim that the account UI frontend formatter “may not support MessageFormat choice syntax” and would render literal `{2,choice,...}` cannot be verified from this diff alone (no UI formatting code shown), so it’s best treated as a concrete compatibility risk to confirm rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] normalizeValue grows a hardcoded per-key allowlist (templateHelp, optimizeLookupHelp, linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*, error-invalid-multivalued-size, email RTL style) so the 'sanitizer' is really a per-key whitelist that will silently pass unsafe content in any future key added to this list. The next contributor who hits a verifier failure will most naturally add another key to this escape hatch rather than fix the message, progressively eroding the security intent of the sanitizer; each entry is also a place the policy and the properties files must stay in sync with no test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `normalizeValue()` with hardcoded, key-specific exceptions (e.g., `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*`, `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, and email RTL style stripping) that modify message contents before sanitization (`verifySafeHtml()` calls `normalizeValue()` prior to `policy.sanitize(value)`). This does create an “escape hatch” mechanism where future verifier failures are likely to be addressed by adding more per-key normalization rules rather than fixing the underlying message content/policy, increasing maintenance/security risk over time. The diff’s new tests cover illegal HTML, no-HTML translations, and changed anchors, but do not specifically assert/lock down behavior of these per-key normalization exceptions, so the concern about policy/properties needing to stay in sync without targeted tests is grounded. However, the claim that it will "silently pass unsafe content" is more speculative; the sanitizer still runs after normalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test asserts the happy path — every new test asserts a violation is reported, and none asserts that a fully valid translated properties file produces an empty messages list, so a false-positive regression in the sanitizer passes the whole suite. The four new tests (verifyDuplicateKeysDetected, verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected, verifyNoHtmlAllowed, verifyNoChangedAnchors) all use hasItem(containsString(...)), which is satisfied even when the verifier spuriously flags every key. I checked VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java — no fixture or assertion anywhere asserts verify() returns an empty list for a clean translation. If a sanitizer/policy regression (e.g., containsHtml() always true, or the unescapeHtml4/replace("<!-- -->","") roundtrip drifting) starts flagging valid translations, the unit tests stay green while the theme-verifier build breaks for every locale contributor. Checked files: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java and all fixtures under misc/theme-verifier/src/test/resources/.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` (sanitizer policies, HTML detection, anchor handling, normalization), but the updated `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest` only contains negative tests that assert an error substring is present (`hasItem(containsString(...))`). In the shown test file changes, there is no test/fixture asserting the happy path (i.e., a valid properties file yields `verify()` returning an empty list). That means a regression that starts flagging valid content could still keep these tests green because they don’t assert absence of messages for a clean input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The normalizeValue() escape-hatch branches (templateHelp's 'CLAIM.<NAME>' removal, optimizeLookupHelp's '<Extensions>' removal, and the {n,choice,...} pattern stripping for error-invalid-multivalued-size and linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit) are exercised by no test in this diff, even though the diff itself depends on them — the properties-file edits to templateHelp and error-invalid-multivalued-size only pass this verifier because of these untested regexes. A regression in any of the three hand-rolled regexes in normalizeValue (e.g., 'CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>' failing to match, or the choice pattern '[^{0-9]+,choice,[^}]*}' regex breaking) flags legitimate translations as 'Illegal HTML' in CI. The keycloak.v3/admin-ui messages_en.properties edited in this very diff contains the new choice-format string that only passes via the third branch — yet no fixture covers a key with {2,choice,...}, so the branch that this PR's own properties change relies on is verified by nothing. Checked: VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java and all five test fixtures — none contains a choice pattern, 'CLAIM.<', '<Extensions>', or an email style attribute.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial normalization escape hatches in `VerifyMessageProperties.normalizeValue()` for `templateHelp`, `optimizeLookupHelp`, and `{n,choice,...}` patterns (including `error-invalid-multivalued-size`). The PR also changes real message strings to include the choice-format (`error-invalid-multivalued-size=... {2,choice,...1<values}`) and adjusts `templateHelp` to contain `CLAIM.<NAME>`, which are exactly the kinds of substrings these regexes are intended to neutralize before the OWASP sanitizer runs. However, the added tests/fixtures (`duplicateKeys_en.properties`, `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, `noHtml_{en,de}.properties`, `changedAnchor_{en,de}.properties`) do not include any `templateHelp`, `<Extensions>`, or `{*,choice,...}` content, so these branches are indeed untested by this diff despite being relied on by the updated properties.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The common-prefix/common-suffix stripping before building the 'Illegal HTML' message throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when the sanitized string is longer than the original with an overlapping prefix and suffix, crashing verify() instead of reporting the violation. A translation containing a raw ampersand (e.g. 'Tom & Jerry') under a key whose English value contains HTML gets its '&' escaped to '&' by the sanitizer; the prefix scan consumes the entire value (start == value.length()) while the suffix scan also finds at least one matching trailing char, so value.substring(start, value.length() - end) is called with start > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException — the Maven mojo dies with a stack trace about substring rather than the 'Illegal HTML in key ...' message the tool exists to produce, and the actual HTML violation is never reported.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), when sanitized != value it computes a common prefix (start) and suffix (end) and then does value.substring(start, value.length() - end) and sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end). If the sanitizer returns a string that starts with the entire original value (so start == value.length()) but is longer and also shares at least 1 trailing character with the original (end > 0), then value.length() - end < start and value.substring(start, value.length() - end) will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, aborting verify(). This crash condition is visible directly in the diff. The finding’s specific '&' -> '&' example is likely wrong because the code unescapes both value (normalizeValue) and sanitized (unescapeHtml4), but the underlying substring bug is still real (e.g., if the sanitizer appends content such as balancing tags).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Deriving the English-file path with the regex replaceAll '_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties' -> '_en.properties' produces a nonexistent path for any file whose locale segment contains digits or that has no locale suffix, and the subsequent failure is thrown as a raw RuntimeException instead of being collected as a verification message. For a locale file like messages_es_419.properties (or a bundle with no locale suffix), the character class [a-zA-Z-_] cannot match '419', the replacement leaves the filename unchanged or yields a path with no messages_en.properties sibling, and new FileInputStream(englishFile) throws — wrapped in a bare RuntimeException, not MojoExecutionException — so the verifier run aborts with an unexpected crash rather than either verifying the file or reporting a clean 'missing English source' finding.

adjudication.rationale: In VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml(), the English bundle path is derived via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. The regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` will not match locale segments containing digits (e.g., `_419.properties`) and also won’t match files with no locale suffix (e.g., `messages.properties`). In those cases the filename is left unchanged, so the code may attempt to open a non-existent “English” file. That `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` failure is caught and rethrown as a raw `RuntimeException`, and `verify()` does not convert it into a collected verification message or a `MojoExecutionException`, so the verifier run can crash unexpectedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] santizeAnchors adds the 'Didn't find anchor tag' message and breaks, but then returns the value with only some anchors stripped, so verifySafeHtml also emits a second misleading 'Illegal HTML' entry pointing at the anchor text itself, and any anchors after the mismatch point are never checked. A translator who modifies an anchor href gets two error entries — the accurate anchor-mismatch one plus a bogus 'Illegal HTML' one naming the <a ...> tag as the illegal content — and additional divergent anchors later in the same string are silently unexamined, misdirecting the contributor fixing the translation.
matched_golden_ids: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a flaw in anchor sanitization/validation when the number of <a> tags differs between English and the translation. The golden issue is that extra anchors in the translation can cause the matcher/group consumption/validation to go wrong, yielding incorrect results. The candidate likewise notes that on an anchor mismatch the logic breaks early, returns partially processed text, and subsequent anchors are never checked—leading to misleading/incorrect validation outcomes. Same underlying problem: mismatched anchor counts cause improper validation behavior.
